negative_findings.description: No dedicated, published time series of financial transaction levy (pénzügyi tranzakciós illeték) revenue broken down by transaction type (card purchase vs cash withdrawal vs transfer) was located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: NAV publishes rules and leaflets, not levy-revenue statistics; searches for 'tranzakciós illeték bevétel statisztika' returned only guidance PDFs, press and secondary figures (e.g. HUF 233bn in 2021 quoted secondarily).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A per-instrument levy breakdown would be the single strongest tax-derived proxy for Hungarian payment volumes; its absence means the proxy must be reconstructed from aggregate budget lines plus statutory rates, or obtained via FOI.

negative_findings.description: The Ministry of Finance / Government monthly central-budget report ('havi költségvetési jelentés', államháztartás központi alrendszerének helyzete) landing page on kormany.hu was not pinned down to a stable URL in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches surfaced only MNB's budget analysis and press coverage; the kormany.hu monthly release page itself did not appear in results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: That monthly release is the fastest official carrier of transaction-levy receipts and is the natural high-frequency series for this cell.

negative_findings.description: For both flagship 2025 cash-related acts (cash-acceptance obligation, Act LXII of 2025; and the free-ATM-withdrawal amendment published mid-December 2025) the exact Magyar Közlöny issue number and page were not confirmed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Press reports confirm publication in Magyar Közlöny with effective dates (2025-07-01 and 2026-02-01 respectively) but no primary gazette citation was retrieved.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Downstream collection needs exact citations to anchor the legal thresholds; without them the facts rest on secondary press.

negative_findings.description: The standalone Financial Arbitration Board domain penzugyibekeltetotestulet.hu was referenced in MNB material but not independently reached in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only mnb.hu/bekeltetes and MNB PDF material were retrieved; the standalone domain is a hypothesis (possibly redirecting to mnb.hu).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Determines whether PBT case data has a separate publication stream to monitor.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian competition-authority (GVH) source specific to interchange/card-scheme fees was surfaced by this cell's queries.
negative_findings.result_summary: Interchange queries returned MNB, EUR-Lex and academic sources only; GVH did not appear.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: GVH case decisions historically shaped Hungarian MIF levels and would add an enforcement-side quantitative source.

brief: Hungary's legislative and fiscal channel for payments intelligence is highly centralised and well-digitised: Magyar Közlöny plus njt.hu carry every binding threshold (transaction levy rates under Act CXVI of 2012, the 2025 merchant cash-acceptance obligation, and the free-ATM-withdrawal limits raised to HUF 300k from February 2026), while parlament.hu bill reasonings expose the fiscal-yield and payment-volume assumptions behind each change. The tax side is strong on rules but weak on published data: NAV issues an annual guidance leaflet on the levy and maintains a public-data/FOI route, but no per-instrument levy revenue series was found, so the levy-as-payment-volume proxy must be rebuilt from budget aggregates plus statutory rates or requested under FOI. The consumer-protection side is the most quantitatively usable: MNB's annual Pénzügyi fogyasztóvédelmi jelentés and the Pénzügyi Békéltető Testület annual reports give consistent multi-year complaint and case counts broken down by product, an indirect read on card, ATM and account usage frictions. Main open gaps are the Ministry of Finance monthly budget release, the MNB supervisory decision register (IFR/payments enforcement), and GVH competition cases on card fees.
